verdict.rationale: Google's own docs describe a Privacy Screen setting that requires device verification (PIN, pattern or biometric) before the app can be used, which directly covers a borrowed phone exposing codes. The only evidence is a single short help-page passage, with nothing hands-on or independent. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, and documentation of which platforms support it and when the app relocks (timeout or backgrounding).

support.subject: As an everyday user, the app itself locks behind biometrics or a PIN, so a borrowed phone doesn't expose my codes

citations.quote: For additional protection, you can turn on Privacy Screen in Google Authenticator. This requires a verification from your device, like a PIN, pattern or biometric prompt, before the app can be used.
